about: The software the game carries from its Unity packages whose licences ask for a notice in every copy, as the packages' own licence files and third-party notices give them (read from unity/Library/PackageCache on 2026-10-25). The credits card (unity/Assets/Scripts/Flow/CreditWords.cs, the settings card's row "Künye") shows them word for word, "©" written "(c)"; tests/Puzzle.Core.Tests/CreditWordsTests.cs holds the card to this record and this record's versions to packages-lock.json beside it. Unity's own packages are under the Unity Companion License, which asks for no notice in a game; packages used only by the Editor (the test frameworks, the IDE bridges, Mono.Cecil, the services' deployment window and its Glob, the light baker's RadeonRays, Bullet and Sobol code in the render pipeline's core) are not in the game and are not listed.

packages.inTheGame: the play statistics' notes, sent only after the player's yes (Statistics/AptabaseNotes.cs)

packages.packageLicence: Unity Companion License (Unity's packaging of it)
packages.from: Third Party Notices.md: Newtonsoft.Json, Json.Net.Unity3D, Newtonsoft.Json-for-Unity, com.newtonsoft.json

receipt reading; asks for no notice

packages.openQuestion: Unity's notice names the Apache License 2.0 but links Google's and Apple's own terms and quotes MIT wording; the card names the Apache licence and its address, not its whole text. Whether the whole Apache text must be shown is the owner's to decide.
